meta.name: Oncovision symptom-and-lab navigator rules
meta.source_document: NICE NG12, Suspected cancer: recognition and referral. Full guideline, National Collaborating Centre for Cancer, June 2015 (final version). Criteria below are paraphrased into structured form from the recommendation boxes; page numbers are PDF pages of that document.
known_limitations: This is the 2015 edition. NICE has revised NG12 since (for example the colorectal pathway now uses the faecal immunochemical test). A clinician must reconcile every rule with the current version before any use beyond research.
It is UK guidance. Referral timeframes and pathways differ in the United States and elsewhere.

The guideline says 'fatigue' in the lung and ovarian recommendations and 'persistent fatigue' in the leukaemia ones. They are treated as one symptom, so the leukaemia and ovarian rules fire slightly more readily than the wording strictly allows.
Examination findings (a lump found by a doctor, an enlarged spleen, a chest X-ray read by a radiologist) cannot be reported by a patient and are excluded except where a report can be uploaded.
design_decisions_for_clinician_review: The lung 'consider an urgent chest X-ray' rule lists a high platelet count among its triggers. It is gated here behind at least one symptom with no known cause. The guideline text does not state that condition, but its lung recommendations are written for people being assessed for lung symptoms, and 3.7% of symptom-free adults over 40 in NHANES have a platelet count above 400, so prompting all of them would be mostly false alarm. This is a deviation from the literal text and a clinician must confirm or reverse it.

Rules that fire from a lab result alone and are stated as recommended in the guideline (iron-deficiency anaemia from 60, anaemia from 60, a positive stool test, a flagged PSA) are NOT gated. By these, 0.7% of symptom-free adults over 40 would be told to talk to a doctor soon and up to about 15% of those over 70 would be told something is worth raising. See experiments/navigator_lab_trigger_burden.py.
meta.review_status: NOT YET REVIEWED BY A CLINICIAN

tiers.talk_soon: Recommended by the guideline: see a doctor promptly. The guideline gives a timeframe of 2 weeks or less.
tiers.worth_raising: The guideline says a clinician may consider acting soon, or advises tests in primary care. Worth raising with a doctor.
tiers.mention: Non-urgent. Worth mentioning at a routine visit.

anaemia_hemoglobin_g_dl.note: World Health Organization definition for adults. Used for 'low haemoglobin' and 'anaemia'.

rules.action: Weight loss with no known reason can be a sign of several cancers. These include bowel, stomach, gullet, lung, prostate, pancreas, kidney and bladder cancer. It can also have other causes. Guidelines say a doctor should look for the cause soon.
rules.source: NG12 2015, symptoms that are not specific to one cancer, p.347

rules.action: Losing your appetite for no known reason can be a sign of several cancers. These include lung, gullet, stomach, bowel, pancreas, bladder and kidney cancer. It can also have other causes. Guidelines say a doctor should look for the cause soon.
rules.source: NG12 2015, symptoms that are not specific to one cancer, p.347
